flag_summary: The same basic Japanese-made pedal appears under multiple marketed names including Herald, Apollo, LRE, Melos, Mica, Monacor and Olson. Minor hardware differences are also reported, so specimens should not be merged solely by circuit family.
The Top Gear Fuzz has a documented relationship to the Guild Grizzly Fuzz, suggesting a marketed-brand/OEM variation that deserves physical specimen comparison before catalog unification.

A three-knob Fuzz Sustain state is documented. Specialist discussion also points to an earlier/two-knob variant associated with the Guild Grizzly Fuzz, making control count and enclosure an immediate identification flag.
Top Gear's 1975 Series-70 line used fibreglass boxes with red faceplates, while earlier pedals used gray or black panels. Determine which dirt models crossed that production transition.
The Zuzz Thainer is extremely rare and has surviving period documentation, making specimen-level production comparison useful even though no formal V2 chronology is currently established.
The combination of a 1965 newspaper-ad trail, an early amp-top Fuzz Blender without MKIV designation, and a later MKIV stompbox strongly supports a deferred family-revision investigation.
The pre-Fuzzmaster box, original green Fuzzmaster, Wildcat and MKIV surviving states provide a strong variation research cluster. Exact chronological boundaries remain open.
